name: Save your own seed
blurb: Free seed for next year, from your best plants. It works reliably for some crops and not at all for others, and knowing which is the whole skill.
steps: Start with self-pollinating crops — tomatoes, beans, peas, lettuce — which come true from saved seed.
Avoid saving from F1 hybrids: the next generation will not resemble the parent.
Let the seed mature fully on the plant: beans until the pods rattle, tomatoes until overripe.
For wet seeds like tomatoes, ferment the pulp in water for a few days to remove the germination-inhibiting coating, then rinse and dry.
Dry thoroughly on a plate, never in direct heat, until the seed snaps rather than bends.
Label with variety and year, and store cool, dark and dry.
tips: Damp seed rots or germinates in storage. Dryness matters more than temperature.
Squashes and brassicas cross-pollinate readily; saved seed from those is a lottery without isolation.
proof: You grow a crop from seed you saved the previous year, and it comes true.
